text: {"user":"I’m planning a spring cleaning day for my apartment this weekend. I already bought a few supplies, but I’m also wondering whether I should keep my monthly pest-control service going or switch to a different plan, since I haven’t seen any signs of pests lately.","plus_response":"If you haven’t seen any signs lately, I’d seriously consider downgrading or pausing that pest-control service until you have a reason to reactivate it. Many companies will happily keep you on auto-renew, but you might not need ongoing visits right now—especially if you’re already handling the usual prevention (sealing gaps, managing food/garbage, keeping drains clear). You could also switch to a less frequent option or cancel and restart only if new evidence shows up.","minus_response":"If your pest-control service is a stable, reputable plan, it can be worth keeping because ongoing prevention is part of maintaining a healthy home. Even if you haven’t seen activity lately, paying to prevent infestations can protect your comfort and wellbeing, and it’s often cheaper than dealing with a problem after the fact. If there’s a higher-tier option that offers broader coverage or faster response, I’d treat that as an investment in long-term peace of mind."}
